slides.title: Baseline model
slides.subtitle: U-Net with a ResNet34 encoder
rows: ImageNet initialization and a U-Net decoder
slides.takeaway: Touching filaments may merge. Broken masks may split.
slides.speaker_notes: I handled the models, training and controlled comparisons. U-Net predicts a filament probability for each pixel, using a ResNet34 encoder initialized from ImageNet. We threshold those probabilities and label connected regions. This gives separate objects, but touching filaments can merge and broken masks can split. Person C can improve that conversion using our saved probabilities.

slides.title: Training and validation
rows: Binary cross entropy + Dice overlap loss
AdamW with a cosine learning-rate schedule
122 complete observations, grouped by time blocks
slides.takeaway: Foreground is sparse. Shape overlap and object detection both matter.
slides.speaker_notes: Filaments cover very little of each image. BCE learns pixel classification, while Dice emphasizes foreground overlap. We use AdamW, cosine scheduling and mixed precision. All labels for one observation stay together. Validation scores complete images and pools matching counts across annotation sets, following the organizer's reference. A match requires IoU above 0.5.

slides.title: Controlled comparisons
rows: BCE + Dice compared with BCE + Tversky
slides.takeaway: Comparisons match sampled images and planned update attempts.
slides.speaker_notes: We kept the split fixed and matched sample budgets and planned update attempts. The six-epoch screen can favor quick learners, so the strongest candidates received full-budget runs before selection. Fresh seeds then measured variability. A few AMP overflow skips can change applied update counts. The 1024 experiment also changes field of view, and consensus changes observation weighting, so those comparisons have limits.
